surface_summary: The case initially appears as a locked-room suicide of Geoffrey Challoner, with no apparent motive and impossible entry. Later, a mysterious murder of Professor McMurray with a rejuvenated body and a missing document puzzles the police. Finally, a staged burglary by Lady Glanedale and the disappearance of boxer Charley Burns add complexity to the detective's investigations.
accepted_facts: Geoffrey Challoner was found shot in a locked library with the door locked from inside
Professor McMurray was found dead with a battered head and appeared younger
Lady Glanedale reported a burglary with stolen jewels and footprints outside her window
Charley Burns disappeared before a major fight and was later found held captive
inferred_conclusions: Challoner committed suicide due to family disputes
The tramp arrested for McMurray's murder was the killer
The burglaries and cattle-maimings were unrelated isolated crimes
mechanism_description: Peters, the butler, forged cheques and murdered Geoffrey Challoner by shooting him from behind, then locked the door using a string and pencil trick to simulate suicide. Sir Jasper Chambers killed Professor McMurray to prevent the serum's revelation, staging the scene to mislead investigators. Lady Glanedale faked a burglary to claim insurance money, creating false footprints and staging the scene.
delivery_path: Peters practiced locking doors with string and pencil to simulate locked-room
Peters shot Challoner from behind while he was absorbed in his passbook
Peters replaced passbook to hide forgery evidence
Sir Jasper Chambers entered McMurray's lab by appointment and killed him with a left-handed blow
Sir Jasper staged forced entry and destroyed evidence including manuscripts
Lady Glanedale created false footprints and staged burglary to claim insurance
Malcolm Sage used photography, fingerprints, and logical deduction to uncover the truth
outcome_result: Malcolm Sage exposes Peters as the murderer of Challoner, Sir Jasper Chambers as McMurray's killer, and Lady Glanedale as a fraudster, restoring justice.

false_assumption.statement: Geoffrey Challoner's death was a straightforward suicide due to family quarrel.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The locked door and presence of a pistol in Challoner's hand suggest suicide, and the family dispute provides a plausible motive. The police and doctor initially confirm the suicide verdict.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It conceals the fact that the door was locked from outside using a string and pencil trick by Peters, who murdered Challoner to cover up forgery.

supporting_points: He had a quarrel with his uncle and was threatened with disinheritance
He returned late at night and was nervous
He had motive to cause distress to Challoner
He was present in the house at the relevant time
false_solution.the_one_flaw: He lacked the opportunity and means to commit the murder in a locked room, and no evidence linked him directly to the crime.

red_herrings.description: Richard Dane's nervous behavior and family quarrel suggest guilt.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: His nervousness was due to stress over his engagement and family disputes, not guilt.

red_herrings.description: A tramp was arrested for McMurray's murder based on possession of the watch and bloodstains.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: The tramp found the watch and was wrongly accused; the real murderer was Sir Jasper Chambers.

closed_circle.rationale: All had access to the crime scenes and potential motives; the locked-room nature and forensic evidence narrowed suspects to those with opportunity and means.

time_anchors: Half-past seven in the morning when body was found
Evening of previous day when quarrel occurred
Early morning of burglary at Lady Glanedale's
time_windows: Between 10 pm and midnight for Challoner's murder
Between dinner and next morning for McMurray's murder
Around 1 am for Lady Glanedale's burglary
Day before fight for Burns's disappearance
access_objects: Cars and bicycles at The Towers

inference_path.observation: The library door was locked from inside with key in place
inference_path.correction: A string and pencil trick was used to lock the door from outside
required_evidence: Marks of string on the bottom edge of the library door
Photograph showing reflection of cord marks under the door

inference_path.observation: Challoner's hand held the pistol unnaturally with second joint on trigger
inference_path.correction: Murderer shot him from behind, causing unnatural hand position
required_evidence: Photograph of Malcolm Sage simulating shooting from behind
Photograph of the wound showing abrasion consistent with head jerk

inference_path.observation: Professor McMurray's body appeared younger than his age
inference_path.correction: Serum experiment caused rejuvenation, motive for murder
required_evidence: Press-cutting of article 'The Dangers of Longevity'

inference_path.observation: Missing document replaced by blank sheets identical in number and quality
inference_path.correction: Theft was planned by someone knowing document's arrival and contents
required_evidence: Note from Sir Lyster Grayne about document placement

inference_path.observation: Footprints and marks on water-pipe at Lady Glanedale's window
inference_path.correction: Footprints made before rain, inconsistent with story
required_evidence: Measurements of footprints and stride length
Rain drops on leaves inside footprints

inference_path.observation: Anonymous letters written on Olympic Script paper
inference_path.correction: Secret ink revealed by heating letters
required_evidence: Letters sealed by vicar and opened with metal plate and flame
Handwriting analysis of letters and sermons

inference_path.correction: Kidnapped by well-dressed men with damaged nose and umbrella
required_evidence: Cigar with red and gold band found at scene

discriminating_test.design: Malcolm Sage reenacted the shooting position and examined the locked door with a mirror and torch to detect marks of the string and pencil trick. He also measured footprints and marks at Lady Glanedale's house, and heated letters to reveal secret ink.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The reenactment revealed that the locked door was manipulated from outside, the footprints were inconsistent with the story, and the letters contained secret ink identifying the true writer.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Physical evidence such as string marks under the door and secret ink appearing on heated letters must be observable and consistent with the reenactment.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed descriptions of the locked door, the position of the body and keys, the marks on the door bottom, and the photographs taken. The secret of the string and pencil trick is explained and illustrated. The inconsistencies in footprints and the secret ink in letters are presented with sufficient clues. The reader could deduce the true culprit by careful attention to these details and logical reasoning.
